item.title: Zenkoji Gokaicho: The Once-in-Seven-Years Grand Pilgrimage — Guide
item.description: The Zenkoji Gokaicho is a grand religious event held at Zenkoji Temple roughly once every seven years, during which a special ‘substitute’ image of the temple’s normally hidden Buddha is revealed, and a tall wooden pillar (kaicho-bashira) is erected in front of the main hall, connected by a sacred cord to the image inside. Millions of pilgrims travel to Nagano over the roughly two-month event to touch the pillar, believed to forge a direct connection with the Buddha and its blessings, making it one of Japan’s largest and most significant recurring religious gatherings.
